definition: Canonical episode = one admitted, fingerprint-tracked unit in a family's canonical manifest, eligible in principle for scoring (regardless of whether any model was ever run against it). Distinguished from: grounded world (a physical/parameterized environment instance, identified by world_id/world_hash), scenario template (a named generator construct, e.g. B-ACQ-1, T-C-BATTERY_ABORT), scenario instantiation (one concrete parameterization of a template before admission), evidence realization/regime (FULL/PHYSICAL_ONLY/DIGITAL_ONLY or similar evidence-delivery condition attached to an episode), model evaluation trajectory (one actual model run against one canonical episode; see evaluated_trajectory_accounting.csv).
discrepancy_explanation: family_counts['A']+family_counts['E'] = 2400+1440 = 3840 is the NOMINAL admitted count for the A/E pool (a_e_pool_manifest.json: episode_count_generated=3840, episode_count_admitted=3840, episode_count_rejected=0). But a_e_pool_manifest.json also records duplicate_fingerprints=42 (42 fingerprint groups covering 87 of the 3840 episodes share a fingerprint with at least one other episode). Collapsing each duplicate group to one canonical representative removes 87-42=45 episodes, giving the TRUE deduped A+E canonical count of 3840-45=3795, which matches source_manifests.A_E.canonical_count=3795 in final_benchmark_manifest_v3.json exactly. final_canonical_total (4075) was built on top of this already-deduped 3795 (via old_final_canonical_total=4009=3795+12(B-legacy)+112(C)+20(D_enterprise)+70(D_physical)), so it is correct; family_counts (4120) is a raw, non-deduped display sum and should never be summed directly.
